messages:
maya: Ran the quantization bench for hopper-7b bring-up across eu-central (H100) and us-west (A100,L4). Comparing FP16 / BF16 / INT8 / FP8. Quick summary below + raw CSV in GDrive.

liam: awesome — any surprising deltas on quality?

maya: TL;DR: INT8 gives ~2.2-2.6x token/sec speedup, FP8 ~3.0-3.4x. Quality cost: INT8 ~+0.4-0.9% ppl increase, FP8 ~+1.1-2.0% on our eval set. BF16 ~= FP16 in quality; BF16 slightly faster on H100 when using fused kernels.

danielle: can you paste the perf table? even a small one.

maya: paste:
```
# per-GPU p50 latency (single-stream), throughput toks/s (batch=8, seq=1024)
H100 (eu-central): FP16 p50=48ms,  tput=850 toks/s
H100 (eu-central): BF16 p50=45ms,  tput=900 toks/s
H100 (eu-central): INT8  p50=28ms,  tput=2050 toks/s
H100 (eu-central): FP8   p50=22ms,  tput=2900 toks/s

A100 (us-west): FP16 p50=62ms,  tput=650 toks/s
A100 (us-west): BF16 p50=60ms,  tput=680 toks/s
A100 (us-west): INT8  p50=35ms,  tput=1500 toks/s
A100 (us-west): FP8   p50=30ms,  tput=1900 toks/s

L4 (us-west): FP16 p50=95ms,  tput=380 toks/s
L4 (us-west): INT8  p50=55ms,  tput=820 toks/s
```

liam: interesting — H100 FP8 is really pulling ahead. what kernels did you use?

maya: details: on H100 used triton fused_attention + custom int8 GEMM path (our marlin-int8 kernel), flash-attn for fp16/bf16. On A100 used cuBLASLt matmul path + optimized flash-attn (less fused benefit than H100). L4 used standard Triton matmul (no int8 specialized).

perf-bot: /benchmark complete — artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/hopper7b/1912345678/*.csv (uploaded) :white_check_mark:

danielle: how about eval numbers? ppl and a couple downstream metrics?

maya: small eval on our 2k-prompt devset (answers/regression suite):
```
Metric baseline (FP16 H100): ppl=12.5, acc@1=73.4%
INT8 H100: ppl=12.9 (+0.4), acc@1=72.9% (-0.5)
FP8  H100: ppl=13.7 (+1.2), acc@1=71.5% (-1.9)
INT8 A100: ppl=13.0 (+0.5), acc@1=72.6% (-0.8)
FP8  A100: ppl=13.6 (+1.1), acc@1=71.8% (-1.6)
```

ryan: are those deltas acceptable for production? we need to gate by per-customer SLOs.

maya: agreed. Proposal: default ship BF16 for new bring-up (lowest risk, small perf bump). Offer INT8 as a "speed-tier" with a quality flag and recommended rollback triggers. FP8 is experimental — enable behind feature flag and only for burst/dedicated pools with QA signoff.

liam: any regional caveats? network latency aside, does eu vs us change model perf?

maya: raw GPU perf stable. primary region delta was image decode + networking for end-to-end latency in our app benchmarks (~8-12ms extra in cross-region). Kernel performance differences mattered more: H100's tensor core layout + our marlin kernels gave larger speedups on H100 vs A100. So routing policy should consider kernel compatibility + quant profile.

danielle: any failure cases in logs? OOM or bad tokens?

maya: a few soft errors on FP8 with extremely long sequences (seq>4k) — kv-cache quant overflow in one run. Added clamp in runtime fixed it. No hard OOMs.

ryan: next steps?

maya: action items:
- (maya) upload cleaned CSV + eval scripts to the GDrive folder and add README with commands used.
- (liam) add INT8/FP8 as separate model variants in catalog with rollback policy + eval thresholds.
- (danielle) run 24h stability run on H100 INT8 in dedicated pool (smoke width 10).
- (ryan) decide whether BF16 default for bring-up by EOD.

liam: noted. thanks maya, this is great. :tada:

perf-bot: scheduled 24h stability run: job_id=stability-1912345678-1

maya: sharing the run command for reproducibility:
```
./run_bench --model hopper-7b --quant INT8 --gpu H100 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --region eu-central --out gs://redwood-bench/hopper7b/1912345678/
```

liam: perfect. ping when the 24h run finishes and we'll review time-series.

maya: will do.
